subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Third-Wave Cafés: Blue Bottle to Intelligentsia
description: A micro-lesson that makes Third-Wave Cafés: Blue Bottle to Intelligentsia usable.

hook.text: In the early 2000s, a new breed of cafés emerged—treating coffee like artisan wine, not a commodity drink.

buildup.text: Blue Bottle, Intelligentsia, Stumptown, and Counter Culture led the movement with single-origin beans and precise brewing.

discovery.text: These shops sourced directly from farmers, roasted in small batches, and trained baristas like professional sommeliers.

twist.text: A pour-over at a third-wave café takes 4 minutes and costs $6–8. The patience required feels radical in a fast-food nation.

climax.text: Third-wave cafés proved that coffee quality had a ceiling only when care stopped. They raised the bar for everyone.

punchline.text: Slower, costlier, intentional. Craft coffee rewrote the American café.

quiz.question: What defines third-wave coffee culture?
options: Treating coffee like artisan wine with single-origin sourcing and precise brewing
